{{technical|date=September 2024}}
{{Short description|Type of fractal dimension}}

In [[fractal geometry]], the '''parabolic Hausdorff dimension''' is a restricted version of the genuine [[Hausdorff dimension]].{{sfn|Taylor|Watson|1985}} Only parabolic cylinders, i. e. rectangles with a distinct non-linear scaling between time and space are permitted as covering sets. It is useful to determine the Hausdorff dimension of self-similar [[stochastic processes]], such as the [[geometric Brownian motion]]{{sfn|Peres|Sousi|2016}} or stable [[Lévy processes]]{{sfn|Kern|Pleschberger|2024}} plus [[Borel measurable]] drift function <math>f</math>.

== Definitions ==

We define the <math>\alpha</math>-parabolic <math>\beta</math>-Hausdorff [[outer measure]] for any set <math>A \subseteq \R^{d+1}</math> as
:<math> \mathcal{P}^\alpha-\mathcal{H}^\beta (A) := \lim_{\delta \downarrow 0} \inf \left \{ \sum_{k=1}^\infty \left | P_k \right |^\beta: A \subseteq \bigcup_{k=1}^\infty P_k, P_k \in \mathcal{P}^\alpha, \left | P_k \right | \leq \delta \right \}.</math>
where the <math>\alpha</math>-parabolic cylinders <math>\left ( P_k \right )_{k \in \mathbb{N}}</math> are contained in
:<math> \mathcal{P}^\alpha := \left \{ [t,t+c] \times \prod_{i=1}^d \left [ x_i, x_i + c^{1/\alpha} \right ]; t, x_i \in \mathbb{R}, c \in (0,1] \right \}.</math>
We define the <math>\alpha</math>-parabolic Hausdorff dimension of <math>A</math> as
:<math>\mathcal{P}^\alpha-\dim A := \inf \left \{ \beta \geq 0: \mathcal{P}^\alpha-\mathcal{H}^\beta (A) = 0 \right \}.</math>
The case <math>\alpha = 1</math> equals the genuine Hausdorff dimension <math>\dim</math>.

== Application ==

Let <math>\varphi_\alpha := \mathcal{P}^\alpha-\dim \mathcal{G}_T(f)</math>. We can calculate the Hausdorff dimension of the fractional Brownian motion <math>B^H</math> of Hurst index <math>1/\alpha = H \in (0,1]</math> plus some measurable drift function <math>f</math>. We get
:<math> \dim \mathcal{G}_T \left (B^H+f \right ) = \varphi_\alpha \wedge \frac{1}{\alpha} \cdot \varphi_{\alpha} + \left (1 - \frac{1}{\alpha} \right) \cdot d </math>
and
:<math> \dim \mathcal{R}_T \left (B^H +f \right ) = \varphi_\alpha \wedge d. </math>
For an isotropic <math>\alpha</math>-stable Lévy process <math>X</math> for <math>\alpha \in (0,2]</math> plus some measurable drift function <math>f</math> we get
:<math> \dim \mathcal{G}_T(X+f) =
\begin{cases}
\varphi_1, & \alpha \in (0,1], \\
\varphi_\alpha \wedge \frac{1}{\alpha} \cdot \varphi_\alpha + \left ( 1 - \frac{1}{\alpha} \right ) \cdot d, & \alpha \in [1,2]
\end{cases}
</math>
and
:<math>
\dim \mathcal{R}_T \left ( X + f \right ) =
\begin{cases}
\alpha \cdot \varphi_\alpha \wedge d, & \alpha \in (0,1], \\
\varphi_\alpha \wedge d, & \alpha \in [1,2].
\end{cases}
</math>

== Inequalities and identities ==

For <math>\phi_\alpha := \mathcal{P}^\alpha-\dim A</math> one has
:<math>
\dim A \leq
\begin{cases}
\phi_\alpha \wedge \alpha \cdot \phi_\alpha + 1 - \alpha, & \alpha \in (0,1], \\
\phi_\alpha \wedge \frac{1}{\alpha} \cdot \alpha + \left ( 1 - \frac{1}{\alpha} \right ) \cdot d, & \alpha \in [1,\infty)
\end{cases}
</math>
and
:<math>
\dim A \geq
\begin{cases}
\alpha \cdot \phi_\alpha \vee \phi_\alpha + \left ( 1 - \frac{1}{\alpha} \right ) \cdot d, & \alpha \in (0,1], \\
\phi_\alpha + 1 - \alpha, & \alpha \in [1,\infty).
\end{cases}
</math>
Further, for the fractional Brownian motion <math>B^H</math> of Hurst index <math>1/\alpha = H \in (0,1]</math> one has
:<math>
\mathcal{P}^\alpha-\dim \mathcal{G}_T \left (B^H \right ) = \alpha \cdot \dim T
</math>
and for an isotropic <math>\alpha</math>-stable Lévy process <math>X</math> for <math>\alpha \in (0,2]</math> one has
:<math>
\mathcal{P}^\alpha-\dim \mathcal{G}_T \left (X \right ) = (\alpha \vee 1) \cdot \dim T
</math>
and
:<math>
\dim \mathcal{R}_T(X) = \alpha \cdot \dim T \wedge d.
</math>
For constant functions <math> f_C </math> we get
:<math>
\mathcal{P}^\alpha-\dim \mathcal{G}_T \left (f_C \right ) = (\alpha \vee 1) \cdot \dim T.
</math>
If <math>f \in C^\beta(T,\mathbb{R}^d) </math>, i. e. <math>f </math> is <math>\beta</math>-[[Hölder continuous]], for <math>\varphi_\alpha = \mathcal{P}^\alpha-\dim \mathcal{G}_T(f)</math> the estimates
:<math>
\varphi_\alpha \leq
\begin{cases}
\dim T + \left ( \frac{1}{\alpha} - \beta \right ) \cdot d \wedge \frac{\dim T}{\alpha \cdot \beta} \wedge d + 1, & \alpha \in (0,1], \\
\alpha \cdot \dim T + (1 - \alpha \cdot \beta) \cdot d \wedge \frac{\dim T}{\beta} \wedge d + 1, & \alpha \in \left [1,\frac{1}{\beta} \right ],\\
\alpha \cdot \dim T + \frac{1}{\beta}(\dim T -1) + \alpha \wedge d + 1, & \alpha \in \left [\frac{1}{\beta}, \infty) \right ]
\end{cases}
</math>
hold.

Finally, for the Brownian motion <math>B</math> and <math>f \in C^\beta \left (T,\mathbb{R}^d \right )</math> we get
:<math>
\dim \mathcal{G}_T(B + f) \leq
\begin{cases}
d + \frac{1}{2}, & \beta \leq \frac{\dim T}{d} - \frac{1}{2d},\\
\dim T + (1 - \beta) \cdot d, & \frac{\dim T}{d} - \frac{1}{2d} \leq \beta \leq \frac{\dim T}{d} \wedge \frac{1}{2},\\
\frac{\dim T}{\beta}, & \frac{\dim T}{d} \leq \beta \leq \frac{1}{2},\\
2 \cdot \dim T \wedge \dim T + \frac{d}{2}, & \text{ else}
\end{cases}
</math>
and
:<math>
\dim \mathcal{R}_T(B + f) \leq
\begin{cases}
\frac{\dim T}{\beta}, & \frac{\dim T}{d} \leq \beta \leq \frac{1}{2},\\
2 \cdot \dim T \wedge d, & \frac{\dim T}{d} \leq \frac{1}{2} \leq \beta,\\
d, & \text{ else}.
\end{cases}
</math>
